transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I spend far too much of the day checking the same folders, drawers, and labeled boxes over and over. I keep making sure my important papers and keepsakes are where I left them, even if I checked them just a few minutes earlier.
What goes through your mind, or what are you worried might happen, if you don't check them?

I worry that I may have accidentally thrown away something important—my husband's old tax papers, for example—or put a family recipe in the wrong box. Even though I know that probably isn't true, the thought keeps bothering me, and I feel terribly careless if I don't go look.
Looking at your daily life, which takes up more of your time and effort: the worrying thoughts themselves, or the physical checking routines?
The checking routines take more time. I keep opening the same drawers and folders, and looking through the labeled boxes, even when I’ve only just checked them.

latest_inference.note: The patient clarified that compulsive checking routines take up more time and effort than the obsessions themselves, specifying predominantly compulsive acts (F42.1) and ruling out mixed obsessional thoughts and acts (F42.2) and obsessive-compulsive personality disorder (F60.5).
